children: JetBlue posted a wider third-quarter loss but revenue climbed despite higher fuel costs.
The carrier posted a loss of $257 million, or 68 cents a share, compared with a loss of $143 million, or 39 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out one-time items, JetBlue posted an adjusted loss of 60 cents a share. Analysts polled by FactSet expected an adjusted loss of 54 cents a share.
Revenue climbed 21% to $2.81 billion, up from $2.32 billion a year earlier but below Wall Street models of $2.83 billion.
JetBlue's average fuel price during the quarter was up 57% at $3.91 a gallon.
The company's stock was up 10.6% at $2.62 in late trading Monday. It closed down 9.7%, tumbling as much as 12% in the regular session, and was on track to close at an all-time low.

The Wall Street Journal reported Friday that a group of JetBlue's senior creditors hired a financial adviser and law firm- a common step for creditors who perceive a risk that a debtor might not be able to fully repay loans in time. JetBlue's bonds also traded down sharply last week.

"We expect further margin expansion in the fourth quarter despite fuel prices forecasted to be 85% higher than in the same period last year," Chief Financial Officer Ursula Hurley said Monday. "Importantly, we believe we have the liquidity and financing options to create a strong bridge to at least $1 EPS and positive free cash flow in 2028."
